Definition: from G4802; mutual questioning, i.e. discussion:--disputation(-ting), reasoning.
BiblicalUsage: The word is the noun behind the disputes in Acts: no small dissension and disputation at Antioch over circumcision, much disputing in the Jerusalem council, and great reasoning among the Jews after Paul's last words in Rome. Each time the question matters, and each time the church has to reason its way through it. The King James text carries this word in all three places, where the older Greek text reads a plainer word for questioning.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the Jerusalem council shows how the church should handle its hardest questions: argue them out in the open, listen to Scripture and to witnesses, and then decide.
